pages.text: "I will not brush! Too much trouble!" Pipo slipped under his bedcovers. Outside the round window, the pen gate was shut. Mom waved a toothbrush. "Brush by the well before bed."
Even when Mom offered it, he pulled the covers over his head. "Can I skip just today?" Mom put out the yard lamp, and Pipo slept without brushing.
But in his sleep—oh? His mouth felt stale and teeth tickled. A piece of dinner cheese was stuck between them. "Something strange between my teeth..." He touched his cheek and woke.
Mom entered with a lamp. "Cheese-thief bugs are hiding between your teeth. Let us chase them away at the well!" She held his hand tightly.
Her words made Pipo imagine the bugs: round little ones sitting on his teeth, hugging cheese crumbs and giggling. "They were making my teeth tickle!"

"Cheese-thief bugs fear exactly one thing—toothpaste foam!" Mom lowered her voice. "The brush is your little shovel, and toothpaste foam is a splash from the well. Brush, brush by the well!" His eyes sparkled.
By the well, Pipo squeezed toothpaste onto the brush and put it in his mouth. Up, down, bubbles foaming. The cheese slipped out, and the bugs fled. "Brush, brush by the well!"
He took a mouthful of tub water, swished, and spat. "Ah—" White teeth! No more tickling. Crouching by the well, hands at his chest, he said, "I chased them away!"
The next morning, Pipo picked up his brush at the well's rim first. "One, sheep say baa, brush, brush! Two, pen gate shut, again! Three, brush up and down!" The sheep had not even called yet.
Mom kissed Pipo's cheek. "Our Pipo has sparkling teeth!" Brushing every day kept bugs away. Showing all his teeth in a smile, Pipo said, "Brush, brush by the well!"
